arxiv-2301-03393.title: Difference of Anisotropic and Isotropic TV for Segmentation under Blur and Poisson Noise
arxiv-2301-03393.creator: Kevin Bui, Yifei Lou, Fredrick Park, Jack Xin
arxiv-2301-03393.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kevin Bui, Yifei Lou, Fredrick Park, Jack Xin. In this paper, we aim to segment an image degraded by blur and Poisson noise. We adopt a smoothing-and-thresholding (SaT) segmentation framework that finds a piecewise-smooth solution, followed by k k -means clustering to segment the image.

arxiv-2310-02891.title: Large-time behavior of two families of operators related to the fractional Laplacian on certain Riemannian manifolds
arxiv-2310-02891.creator: Effie Papageorgiou
arxiv-2310-02891.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Effie Papageorgiou. This note is concerned with two families of operators related to the fractional Laplacian, the first arising from the Caffarelli-Silvestre extension problem and the second from the fractional heat equation. They both include the Poisson semigroup. We show that on a complete, connected, and non-compact Riemannian manifold of non-negative Ricci curvature, in both cases, the solution with L 1 L^{1} initial data behaves asymptotically as the mass times the fundamental solution.

arxiv-2403-18091.title: The Flying Sidekick Traveling Salesman Problem with Multiple Drops: A Simple and Effective Heuristic Approach Journal: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
arxiv-2403-18091.creator: Sarah K. Schaumann, Abhishake Kundu, Juan C. Pina-Pardo, Matthias Winkenbach, Ricardo A. Gatica, Stephan M. Wagner, Timothy I. Matis
arxiv-2403-18091.description: Abstract We study the FSTSP-MD ( FSTSP-MD ), a multi-modal last-mile delivery model where a single truck and a single drone cooperatively deliver customer packages. In the FSTSP-MD , the drone can be launched from the truck to deliver multiple packages before it returns to the truck for a new delivery operation.

arxiv-2406-06152.title: On the Complexity of Inverse Bivariate Multi-unit Assignment Valuation Problems
arxiv-2406-06152.creator: Kristóf Bérczi, Lydia Mirabel Mendoza-Cadena
arxiv-2406-06152.description: Abstract Inverse and bilevel optimization problems play a central role in both theory and applications. These two classes are known to be closely related due to the pioneering work of Dempe and Lohse (2006), and thus have often been discussed together ever since. In this paper, we consider inverse problems for multi-unit assignment valuations.

arxiv-2410-20896.title: BSD: a Bayesian framework for parametric models of neural spectra
arxiv-2410-20896.creator: Johan Medrano, Nicholas A. Alexander, Robert A. Seymour, Peter Zeidman
arxiv-2410-20896.description: Abstract The analysis of neural power spectra plays a crucial role in understanding brain function and dysfunction. While recent efforts have led to the development of methods for decomposing spectral data, challenges remain in performing statistical analysis and group-level comparisons. Here, we introduce Bayesian Spectral Decomposition (BSD), a Bayesian framework for analysing neural spectral power.

arxiv-2507-20369.title: Clustering by Attention: Leveraging Prior Fitted Transformers for Data Partitioning
arxiv-2507-20369.creator: Ahmed Shokry, Ayman Khalafallah
arxiv-2507-20369.description: Abstract Clustering is a core task in machine learning with wide-ranging applications in data mining and pattern recognition. However, its unsupervised nature makes it inherently challenging. Many existing clustering algorithms suffer from critical limitations: they often require careful parameter tuning, exhibit high computational complexity, lack interpretability, or yield suboptimal accuracy, especially when applied to large-scale datasets.

arxiv-2508-02353.title: Cohomologically calibrated affine connections and the Einstein condition on S 2 × T 2 S^{2}\times T^{2}
arxiv-2508-02353.creator: Alexander Pigazzini, Magdalena Toda
arxiv-2508-02353.description: Abstract This paper applies the recently developed framework of cohomologically calibrated affine connections to the fundamental problem of constructing non-Riemannian Einstein manifolds. In this framework, the torsion of a connection is intrinsically related to the global topology of the manifold, represented by the de Rham cohomology class specified by a set of real parameters.

arxiv-2508-13984.title: The AI-Fraud Diamond: A Novel Lens for Auditing Algorithmic Deception
arxiv-2508-13984.creator: Benjamin Zweers, Diptish Dey, Debarati Bhaumik
arxiv-2508-13984.description: Abstract As artificial intelligence (AI) systems become increasingly integral to organizational processes, they introduce new forms of fraud that are often subtle, systemic, and concealed within technical complexity. This paper introduces the AI-Fraud Diamond, an extension of the traditional Fraud Triangle that adds technical opacity as a fourth condition alongside pressure, opportunity, and rationalization.

arxiv-2511-13681.title: Damping of phonons in one-dimensional quantum fluids
arxiv-2511-13681.creator: Federica Cataldini, Nataliia Bazhan, João Sabino, Philipp Schüttelkopf, Mohammadamin Tajik, Frederik S. Møller, Si-Cong Ji, Sebastian Erne, Igor Mazets, Jörg Schmiedmayer
arxiv-2511-13681.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Federica Cataldini, Nataliia Bazhan, João Sabino, Philipp Schüttelkopf, Mohammadamin Tajik, Frederik S. Møller, Si-Cong Ji, Sebastian Erne, Igor Mazets, Jörg Schmiedmayer. Collective excitations in one-dimensional (1D) quantum fluids are expected to propagate almost without dissipation. Here we directly excite phonon modes in a weakly interacting 1D Bose gas and study their time evolution. In the linear response regime, damping is surprisingly fast and quantitatively follows the non-analytic scaling Γ k ∝ k 3 / 2 \Gamma_{k}\propto k^{3/2} predicted by Andreev’s hydrodynamic description.

pmc-10507147.title: Combined influence of immigration status and income on cervical cancer screening uptake
pmc-10507147.creator: Jeanne Sassenou, Virginie Ringa, Marie Zins, Anna Ozguler, Sylvain Paquet, Henri Panjo, Jeanna-Eve Franck, Gwenn Menvielle, Laurent Rigal
pmc-10507147.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The regular performance of Pap tests for cervical cancer screening reduces this disease's incidence and mortality. Income inequalities have been reported for this screening, partly because in some countries women must advance or even pay out-of-pocket costs. Because immigrant status is also associated with low Pap test uptake, we aimed to analyze the combined impact of immigrant status and low income on cervical cancer underscreening.

pmc-10715021.title: The Challenging Path to Diagnosing Extraintestinal Amoebiasis: A Case Report of an HIV-Infected Patient
pmc-10715021.creator: Xiaofeng Li, Cha Chen, Luyuan Tong, Qun Gao, Wenxian Chen, Guangde Zhou, Zhaowei Tong, Weihong Wang
pmc-10715021.description: BackgroundAmoebiasis, an infectious disease caused by the parasitic protozoan E. histolytica, is easily misdiagnosed due to its declining incidence and atypical symptoms.Case PresentationA 31-year-old male presented to the hospital with dyspnea and inability to lie flat. Imaging studies indicated a large amount of pleural effusion on the right side and multiple huge cysts in the liver.

pmc-11436800.title: Massively parallel characterization of insulator activity across the genome
pmc-11436800.creator: Clarice K. Y. Hong, Yawei Wu, Alyssa A. Erickson, Jie Li, Arnold J. Federico, Barak A. Cohen
pmc-11436800.description: A key question in regulatory genomics is whether cis-regulatory elements (CREs) are modular elements that can function anywhere in the genome, or whether they are adapted to certain genomic locations. To distinguish between these possibilities we develop MPIRE (Massively Parallel Integrated Regulatory Elements), a technology for recurrently assaying CREs at thousands of defined locations across the genome in parallel.

pmc-12560902.title: Refining Electronic Tagging of Marine Animals: Computational Fluid Dynamics and Pelagic Sharks
pmc-12560902.creator: Tobias C Maillard, Francesco Garzon, Lucy A Hawkes, Gavin R Tabor, Matthew J Witt, Laura Calvillo, Johnny Roughan
pmc-12560902.description: Simple SummaryScientists commonly attach electronic tags to marine animals to study their movements and behavior in the ocean. However, these tags may have consequences by making it harder for animals to swim efficiently, potentially harming their recovery and survival while also affecting the quality of research data collected.

pmc-12766722.title: Controlling Intramolecular Rotation with Five-Membered Heterocycles Facilitates the Design of Highly Cell-Permeable Xanthene-Based Fluorogenic Probes
pmc-12766722.creator: Shahi Imam Reja, Yuichiro Hori, Youhei Takeda, Miyako Nishiura, Masafumi Minoshima, Kazuya Kikuchi
pmc-12766722.description: Fluorogenic probes are invaluable tools in biology and medicine, offering high sensitivity and background-free imaging. However, achieving a high signal-to-noise ratio, target specificity, and robust cell permeability in wash-free imaging remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a new class of fluorogenic fluorophores engineered by incorporating five-membered heterocycles such as furan or thiophene at 9-position of the xanthene core.

pmc-13246982.description: In Uruguay, Pinus taeda is the dominant conifer in industrial plantations, generating large volumes of knot-containing offcuts during processing. These residues are highly enriched in extractives, offering opportunities for valorization within a circular bioeconomy. This study examined the recovery of bioactive compounds from P.

pmc-13269123.title: Nonlinear periodic orbit solutions and their bifurcation structure at the origin of soliton hopping in coupled microresonators
pmc-13269123.creator: Savyaraj Deshmukh, Aleksandr Tusnin, Alexey Tikan, Tobias J Kippenberg, Tobias M Schneider
pmc-13269123.description: Coupled-microresonator systems, enabled by recent breakthroughs in the nanofabrication of low-loss integrated photonic microresonators, deliver significant performance benefits for coherent frequency comb generation beyond single resonators. They also display emergent nonlinear phenomena including soliton hopping—a dynamic process in which solitons periodically transit between coupled resonators.

pmc-13457238.title: One of These Things Is Not Like the Others: Disentangling the Concepts of Range of Motion Versus Flexibility, and Flexibility Training Versus Stretching
pmc-13457238.creator: José Afonso, Anthony J Blazevich, David George Behm, Markus Tilp, Konstantin Warneke
pmc-13457238.description: In this Current Opinion, we revisit key terminological distinctions in sports sciences, emphasizing the implications of conflating related but distinct concepts, particularly range of motion (ROM) versus flexibility and flexibility training versus stretching. While often used interchangeably, these terms represent nuanced constructs with distinct physiological and practical implications. ROM encompasses both modifiable (e.g.

pmc-13545029.title: Less cooperative belowground plant mutualists negatively affect aboveground herbivore growth and survival
pmc-13545029.creator: Annaliese H. Wargin, Katy D. Heath, Jennifer A. Lau, Adam G. Dolezal, Alexandra N. Harmon-Threatt
pmc-13545029.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Resource mutualists like nitrogen (N)-fixing rhizobia can improve the quality of plants available to higher trophic levels, particularly primary consumers like insect herbivores. However, there is substantial variation in mutualist quality. How this variation in mutualist quality affects higher trophic levels, such as herbivores, is unclear, as high-quality resource mutualists could increase both leaf nutrient content, which should improve herbivore growth, but also plant chemical defenses, which are expected to negatively impact herbivores.

pmc-13649954.title: Federal Protections for Farmworker Health in the United States: A Scoping Review of Three Decades of Research
pmc-13649954.creator: Kaitlyn Alvarez Noli, Stephane Labossiere, Becca Berkey, Joseph G Grzywacz
pmc-13649954.description: ObjectivesThis scoping review characterizes the scope, methods, and framing of empirical research evaluating the Field Sanitation Standard (FSS) and Worker Protection Standard (WPS) of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the U.S. Department of Labor respectively.MethodsFollowing the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, we identified empirical studies (1990–2024) assessing elements of either the FSS or WPS.

pmc-13656451.title: Beyond risk: resilience portfolios and youth mental health
pmc-13656451.creator: Kimberly J. Mitchell, Victoria Banyard
pmc-13656451.description: BackgroundGiven concerns about the mental health of young people, there has been a growing body of research aimed at understanding strengths, resilience, and protective factors. The current study utilizes latent profile analysis to examine different combinations of strengths. Group differences on demographics, social determinants of health (SDoH), and mental health indices are examined across the identified latent classes.
